name: gizza-ai/vector-similarity
summary: Rank nearest vectors by cosine, dot product and distance metrics.

tool.description: Compare a query vector with a list of candidate vectors and return the nearest neighbours. Accepts comma, whitespace or JSON-array-like numeric vectors; candidates may be labelled with `label: values`. metric chooses cosine, cosine_distance, dot, euclidean, manhattan, chebyshev or hamming. top_k limits returned neighbours, normalize optionally scales vectors to unit length, hamming_tolerance treats close numeric coordinates as equal, decimals controls score precision, show_all_metrics includes the companion metric columns, and output selects table, JSON or CSV. Runs locally.

decimals.description: Decimal places for floating-point scores in table, CSV and JSON output, from 0 to 12. Hamming counts remain integers.

hamming_tolerance.description: For Hamming distance, coordinates whose absolute difference is at most this tolerance count as equal. Default 0 for exact numeric equality.

metric.description: Ranking metric: cosine similarity, cosine_distance, dot product, Euclidean, Manhattan, Chebyshev or Hamming distance. Similarity metrics rank higher first; distance metrics rank lower first.

normalize.description: L2-normalize the query and each candidate before scoring. Useful when vector direction matters more than magnitude; zero vectors then fail clearly.

output.description: Output format: aligned text table (default), JSON or CSV.

query.description: Query vector to compare against, as numbers separated by commas, spaces or JSON-array punctuation. Example: 3, 2, 1.

show_all_metrics.description: Include cosine, dot, Euclidean, Manhattan, Chebyshev and Hamming columns beside the ranking metric. Turn off for a compact result.

top_k.description: Maximum number of nearest neighbours to return, from 1 to 2000. Values above the candidate count return every candidate.

vectors.description: Candidate vectors, one per line. Prefix a label with 'label: values'; otherwise labels v1, v2, ... are assigned. Every vector must have the same number of dimensions as query.
